I will keep things simple and familiar. In Quzhou County, my land, water, and weather fit the usual wheat and summer maize rotation best, and at my age I would rather run a steady system I know well than take on a risky new crop. I will put most of my land into winter wheat followed by summer maize, because that gives me stable grain, uses the machinery and habits I already have, and matches the local growing season. If I keep a small piece for peanuts, it is only to spread a little risk and leave myself some cash flexibility, but I will not make the farm complicated. I will use improved or hybrid seed where it helps yield and standability, apply fertilizer at moderate rates instead of chasing the maximum, irrigate when the crop really needs it, and spray only as needed for common weeds, insects, and disease. For tillage, I will mostly use rotary tillage because it is practical for me, fast enough, and easier to manage than deep ploughing every year.
